title: DeactivateFlow
wrapsNative: sheet(isPresented:content:) with presentationDetents and interactiveDismissDisabled, a ScrollView and VStack, Label
summary: A recipe, not a component: confirm a reversible pause (a partnership, a tracker, a person) in a sheet that says where to turn it back on, lists what changes meanwhile and can record a reason; the same sheet confirms reactivation.
whenToUse: When an action stops something working but keeps its data, such as deactivating a user, pausing a partnership or turning off an integration, and when turning it back on.
whenNotToUse: When the action deletes data or cannot be undone, use a destructive confirmationDialog or a delete flow with MonarchTypeToConfirmInput. When the change is trivial and instant to reverse, change it directly with a Toggle and no confirmation. With nothing to list and no reason to ask, a plain confirmationDialog is enough.
api: MonarchTextField("Reason (optional)", text: $reason, helper: "Kept with the change history.")
MonarchButton("Deactivate", variant: .primary, isLoading: isWorking, fullWidth: true, action: confirm)

states.name: deactivate
states.description: Title "Deactivate …?", the description that nothing is deleted, the line saying where to reactivate, what changes while it is deactivated, the optional reason and Deactivate.

states.name: reactivate
states.description: Title "Reactivate …?", what changes once it is back, and Reactivate; no reversibility line.

states.name: working
states.description: The confirm button shows its spinner and the sheet cannot be swiped away.

states.name: failed
states.description: A thrown error goes in a danger MonarchInlineNotice above the buttons; the sheet stays open so the person can retry.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component in the theme: the title style, body text, MonarchConsequenceList with its kind icons, MonarchTextField, a full-width primary MonarchButton and a ghost Cancel. Nothing uses the danger colours, because nothing is lost.
platformNotes: The web DeactivateFlow is a warning-toned ConfirmDialog. The iOS system alert and confirmation dialog cannot hold a consequence list or a text field, so the recipe uses a sheet with a primary (not destructive) confirm button, since nothing is deleted; Monarch has no warning button variant. For a pause with no consequences and no reason, use confirmationDialog with a non-destructive button instead. The web's mode, subject and reactivateFrom props become the app's own state and strings in the recipe.
accessibility: The title has the header trait.
The reversibility line is a Label whose icon is read with its text.
MonarchConsequenceList reads each consequence with its kind, not by icon colour alone.
The reason field is a MonarchTextField with its label and helper text.
Buttons are MonarchButtons with 44-point touch targets and a busy state while working; the sheet cannot be dismissed by swiping while the request runs.
edgeCases: If the request fails, keep the sheet open with the error so the person can retry or cancel.
Send the reason with the request only when it is not empty.
Reactivation can be offered from the same place the line names, so the promise in the line is true.
